title: KAFKA-20691: PersisterStateBatchCombiner.combineStateBatches() with an event-driven sweep-line
body:
Fix https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-20691

 Replaces the iterative TreeSet-based PersisterStateBatchCombiner merge
logic with a sweep-line implementation. The new approach models state
batches as start/end events, tracks active (deliveryCount,
deliveryState) priorities with a counted TreeMap, and emits the winning
non-overlapping ranges while preserving gaps.

Before:

  - Iterative overlap merging with repeated candidate search/reinsert
cycles.    - Worst-case behavior can grow beyond a single sort/sweep due
to repeated TreeSet mutations and rescans.

How:

- Emit (firstOffset, BEGIN) and (lastOffset + 1, END) for each pruned
batch.
- Sort events by (offset asc, END before BEGIN).
- Sweep events;
- At every offset advance, emit a slice with the heap-top's (state,
count); coalesce contiguous slices with identical (state, count).

Result

- Worst case: O(n^2) went to O((n + k) log p)
  - n = number of input batches
  - k = number of emitted/transition ranges
  - p = number of distinct active (deliveryCount, deliveryState)
priorities

- Public API unchanged.

Reviewers: Sushant Mahajan <smahajan@confluent.io>, Andrew Schofield
 <aschofield@confluent.io>
